land.text: the Suebian kingdom that 'appeared' in northeastern Pannonia after Attila's death in 453 under Hunimund and Alaric; the Marcomanni page does not say the Marcomanni became it

successors.note: A bridge, not a statement of the page. eu-06-x lists 'the Suebi of the Danube' among its additions; the slug is a suggestion.

correction.text: Boiohaemum, 'a forested region later associated with Bohemia', where Maroboduus 'led the Marcomanni to the area later known as Bohemia'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'received a new king named Maroboduus' in 9 BC, settled in Boiohaemum in 9-7 BC, and by 6 BC 'had established a powerful kingdom there' (Marcomanni page); Maroboduus page: 'in about 9 BC, Maroboduus returned to Germania and became ruler of his people' and 'organized a confederation of several neighboring Germanic tribes'. The confederation's lands beyond Bohemia are not named on either page. No area.

correction.text: Bohemia (Boiohaemum, no page gives it to anyone else) with the Morava-Cusus area, where the displaced Marcomanni were 'placed under the control of the Quadian king Vannius'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Catualda deposed Maroboduus in 19 AD, Vibilius of the Hermunduri deposed Catualda, and 'the displaced Marcomanni were placed under the control of the Quadian king Vannius'; Vannius was deposed in 50/51 by Vibilius and the Hermunduri with the Lugii. [Fix 2026-10-19: Bohemia stays Marcomannic. The Marcomanni page does not say who held Bohemia after 19 (the Catualda page does not either); the Tacitus passage of about 100 AD it quotes ('their very territory, from which the Boii were driven in a former age, was won by valour') puts the Marcomanni on the former Boii land, Bohemia, and the page has the Marcomanni kingdom 'now came to stretch into this Danubian area, probably including areas in Moravia and Lower Austria'. The 19 loss and 51 gain of Bohemia (counterpart Hermunduri) are dropped. Moravia is drawn as a vassal area under the Quadi from 20 to 50 (vassal_start/vassal_end, counterpart quadi); the extent is the researcher's reading and the shape is soft.]

correction.text: Bohemia and Moravia, the Marcomanni's land north of the Danube (the Roman plan of Marcomannia covered 'Moravia, Slovakia, and Bavaria north of Danube')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, deliberately thin: the pages place the Marcomanni north of the Danube from the time of Vannius to the Marcomannic Wars (166-180, 'status quo ante bellum', Roman plans to annex Marcomannia 'abandoned') and give no map for 51-165 or after 180. The Marcomanni page: in the third century the Suebian 'center of activity shifted east' towards the Slovakia-Hungary border, and Gallienus (253-268) 'settled the Marcomanni within the Roman province of Pannonia Superior'; both are left undrawn. Treat 51-453 as one soft shape; no area is given.

region.text: Boiohaemum, 'a forested region later associated with Bohemia', where Maroboduus 'led the Marcomanni to the area later known as Bohemia'

ledger.note: 9 BC: the Marcomanni, under the new king Maroboduus, settle in Bohemia. 'received a new king named Maroboduus' after a major defeat by Rome; they settled in Boiohaemum in 9-7 BC and by 6 BC he 'had established a powerful kingdom there'. The year is that of the new king; the move to Bohemia spans 9-7 BC. Maroboduus page: 'in about 9 BC' he 'became ruler of his people'.

region.text: the area 'between the Morava and "Cusus" rivers' to which the displaced Marcomanni were moved under the Quadian king Vannius

ledger.note: 20: the displaced Marcomanni come under the Quadian king Vannius. Marcomanni page: the displaced Marcomanni 'were moved by the Romans to an area near the Danube, between the Morava and "Cusus" rivers' and 'placed under the control of the Quadian king Vannius'; the page gives the year 19 for the fall of Maroboduus and Catualda and no separate year for the move, the Vannius page has his rule from 20, which the quadi dossier uses. Written from the vassal's side: Moravia is the Marcomanni's land held under Quadian lordship, the mirror of quadi /ledger/1 (vassal_start, counterpart marcomanni). [Fix 2026-10-19: was a 'gain' from the Quadi at conf 1; both dossiers drew Moravia as their own land.]

region.text: the area 'between the Morava and "Cusus" rivers' to which the displaced Marcomanni were moved under the Quadian king Vannius

ledger.note: 50: Vannius is deposed and the Marcomanni leave Quadian lordship. Marcomanni page: Vannius 'was himself eventually also deposed by Vibilius and the Hermunduri', 'working together with the Lugii from the north, in 50/51 AD'; the page does not say what became of the Marcomanni then and adds that the Marcomanni kingdom 'now came to stretch into this Danubian area, probably including areas in Moravia and Lower Austria'. 50 matches quadi /ledger/3 (vassal_end, counterpart marcomanni). [Fix 2026-10-19: replaces the 51 'gain' of Bohemia and Moravia from the Hermunduri, which no page supports.]

region.text: the Danube frontier at Carnuntum, where the Marcomanni 'defeated a Roman force of 20,000', and Marcomannic Moravia, into which Roman forces crossed in 172

ledger.note: 169: the Marcomanni cross the Danube. Under Ballomar they 'crossed the Danube, and defeated a Roman force of 20,000 near Carnuntum' after Marcus resumed the campaign in autumn 169 (the page does not date the crossing; a footnote says the siege of Aquileia is dated 167 or 170); they were 'ravaging Noricum'. The wars began 'about AD 166' (infobox).

region.text: the Danube frontier at Carnuntum, where the Marcomanni 'defeated a Roman force of 20,000', and Marcomannic Moravia, into which Roman forces crossed in 172

ledger.note: 180: Commodus makes peace. 'Commodus negotiated peace with the Marcomanni and Quadi'; infobox 'Roman victory', 'Status quo ante bellum' and 'Roman plans to annex Sarmatia (Hungarian Plain) and Marcomannia (Moravia, Slovakia, and Bavaria north of Danube) abandoned'. In 172 'the campaign resulted in the subjugation of the Marcomanni and their allies, the Naristi (or Varistae) and the Cotini'; in 177 'the Quadi rebelled, soon joined by the Marcomanni'. The Marcomanni page adds 'Roman garrisons stationed in both territories' in 180, which the Marcomannic Wars page does not confirm.

region.text: Bohemia and Moravia, the Marcomanni's land north of the Danube (the Roman plan of Marcomannia covered 'Moravia, Slovakia, and Bavaria north of Danube')

ledger.note: 453: the Marcomanni vanish from the page as a polity. 'after he died in 453 a Suebian kingdom appeared' under Hunimund and Alaric in northeastern Pannonia; the page says the Marcomanni 'might have been present under that name' at the Catalaunian Plains in 451 and lists a tribune of the Marcomanni in the Notitia Dignitatum around 420. The end year is the researcher's bridge: no page gives an end. [Fix 2026-10-19: the Hunimund page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunimund) puts Hunimund's kingdom 'somewhere near the old settlement area of the Marcomanni and the Quadi', treats the Suebi and Marcomanni as separate groups, does not mention Pannonia Valeria, and dates Nedao to 454 and Bolia to 469; 453 stays a conf-1 bridge.]

wars.name: Augustus's planned campaign against Maroboduus
wars.outcome: Augustus 'aimed to eliminate the last power center in Germania' in AD 6, but a Pannonian revolt stopped the planned attack; Maroboduus stayed neutral and Tiberius was forced 'to conclude a treaty with Maroboduus and to recognize him as king' (Maroboduus page, undated).
wars.note: Maroboduus page: 'Augustus planned in 6 AD to destroy the kingdom of Maroboduus'.

wars.name: War between Arminius and Maroboduus
wars.outcome: War broke out in 17 AD between the two coalitions; after an indecisive battle Maroboduus withdrew into the forests of Bohemia in 18, and was deposed by Catualda in the next year; Tiberius detained him 18 years at Ravenna (died 37).
wars.note: Marcomanni page: 'war broke out among these two alliances of Germanic peoples' (17), 'withdrew into the hilly forests of Bohemia' (18), Catualda 'deposed' him (19).

wars.name: Domitian's Pannonian campaign against the Marcomanni
wars.outcome: Domitian 'was then defeated by the Marcomanni' after a campaign into Pannonia (89 AD).
wars.note: No territorial change on the page.

wars.name: Marcomannic Wars

zones.text: the Danube frontier at Carnuntum, where the Marcomanni 'defeated a Roman force of 20,000', and Marcomannic Moravia, into which Roman forces crossed in 172

wars.outcome: Roman victory, 'status quo ante bellum': the Marcomanni and Quadi crossed the Danube (about 169) and were subjugated in 172 and 174; the Quadi rebelled in 177, joined by the Marcomanni; Rome won near Laugaricio (Trencin) in 179; Commodus made peace in 180 and the plans for Marcomannia and Sarmatia were abandoned.
wars.note: The Marcomanni page dates the crossing to '167 or 169' and the Roman declaration of a new war to 177.

wars.name: Diocletian's Marcomannic triumph
wars.outcome: Diocletian 'claimed a triumph over the Marcomanni in 299 AD'.
wars.note: No territorial change on the page.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary north of the Danube; the Roman frontier is the Danube.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks. Three pages opened. The Marcomanni are known on these pages mainly from the Roman side: no page gives their land except Bohemia (Maroboduus) and the Roman plan of Marcomannia (Moravia, Slovakia and Bavaria north of the Danube); the 19-50 and 51-453 shapes are therefore soft guesses (confidence 1) and the end year 453 is bridged from the appearance of a Suebian kingdom in Pannonia. No capital is drawn: the page names 'Buiaimon' as Maroboduus's royal seat (citing Strabo), the Maroboduus page names none, and no coordinates are given. No ruler list: kings named are Maroboduus (about 9 BC-19), Catualda (19), Vannius (Quadian king over the Marcomanni 19-50/51), Ballomar (mid-160s). The roman-empire dossier has the Marcomannic Wars as a war with no events; the contest here is the only contest event. Counterparts that need dossiers: 'quadi' (written in this batch if reached), 'Hermunduri', 'danubian-suebi' (eu-06-x). Wikidata id unknown. Gazetteer: 'Pannonia' and 'Noricum' are not region names; Carnuntum is a place. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the 20 event is now a vassal_start (counterpart quadi, Moravia) with a vassal_end in 50, mirroring quadi /ledger/1 and /ledger/3. The 19 loss and 51 gain of Bohemia from the Hermunduri are dropped: the Marcomanni page, the Catualda page and the Hunimund page (all opened) do not say the Hermunduri took Bohemia, and Tacitus's c. 100 remark on the former Boii land (Marcomanni page) argues the opposite; hermunduri /ledger/1-2 (19 gain, 51 loss of Bohemia, counterpart marcomanni) are therefore unmirrored and should be dropped or sourced by their owner. Vassal events follow the vassal-side reading used by kingdom-of-cappadocia (the vassal's own dossier names the overlord); the schema text reads them as the overlord's. 453 is still a bridge: the Hunimund page treats the Suebi and Marcomanni as separate groups.]
